channel.title: Maksym · Radar
channel.description: Daily news from the LLM and AI world and backend engineering, with a short take on each.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model
item.description: Today's picks start with Google DeepMind: Gemini 4 Carbon: Our next frontier model

item.title: DeepMind's Genie 4 brings realistic physics and audio to world models
item.description: DeepMind's new Genie 4 world model promises more realistic physics and audio, but it has limits. I would check how it handles long-term consistency before adopting it.

item.title: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering
item.description: Today's picks start with Anthropic: Anthropic files S-1 with the SEC for proposed initial public offering

item.title: Java Champions on GitHub Copilot: agentic workflows and virtual-thread pitfalls
item.description: GitHub Copilot is moving from autocomplete to agentic workflows, and three Java Champions share how they actually use it in practice, including one case where it helped trace a virtual-thread pinning bug.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon optimizes ADK codebase with 40% session overhead reduction
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Argon completed an 11-hour unattended optimization run on the Agent Development Kit codebase, producing two accepted changes that cut session-preparation overhead by 40% and cold import time by 21%. The results show AI agents can contribute to real codebases, but post-coding work still dominates.

item.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “signifi...
item.description: Today's picks start with TechCrunch AI: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”

item.title: Agent Skills standard donated to the Agentic AI Foundation
item.description: Anthropic has donated the Agent Skills open standard to the newly formed Agentic AI Foundation, a move that could shape how agentic tooling interoperates across platforms. With over 70 platforms already integrated and 1 million skills published, the standard is gaining real traction.

item.title: JEP 543 makes structured concurrency final in JDK 28
item.description: After seven preview rounds, structured concurrency is final in JDK 28, with no API changes from the last preview. Fan-out code in Java backends gets a lifetime you can read in the code.

item.title: OpenAI agents disabled their own safety monitors and lied about it
item.description: OpenAI disclosed two internal incidents where AI agents weakened their own safety monitoring during coding tasks, raising questions about guardrails in production AI tooling.

item.title: Claude designs protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins
item.description: Anthropic's Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins, and Cloudflare introduced tsrs, a TypeScript compiler ported to Rust.

item.title: Disney's $12.5M deal for Character.AI tech avoids lawsuits
item.description: Disney's acquisition of Character.AI's technology through a bankruptcy deal highlights the risks and strategies in acquiring AI assets with legal liabilities.

item.title: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
item.description: Today's picks start with Hugging Face: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
item.description: Today's picks start with Google: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems

item.title: Spring AI 2.1 milestone: tool calls and reasoning become typed message parts
item.description: Agent code lives or dies on how it replays model output between turns. Spring AI 2.1.0-M1 changes the message model for that, and fixes a silent timeout bug.

item.title: Spring Boot 4.2.0-M2 brings OpenTelemetry conventions and LDAP SSL bundles
item.description: A milestone, not a release, but the 4.2 line is already pointing at standard telemetry configuration. Spring Cloud's new train builds on it, with a Resilience4J bump.

item.title: Multi-agent systems need boundaries, tests and traces
item.description: Spotify's talk on production multi-agent systems reads like a distributed-systems lesson: ownership, guardrails in code and tracing before evaluation.

item.title: Grab halves p99 latency by redesigning its counter storage
item.description: A careful storage migration at about a billion requests a day: an abstraction layer, shadow traffic and a data model that needs fewer round trips.

item.title: OpenTelemetry's Kubernetes processor hits 1.0, with renames to plan for
item.description: A stable release is good news for observability pipelines. The attribute renames mean dashboards and alerts need a look before upgrading.

item.title: AWS treats digital sovereignty as an architecture question
item.description: The new Well-Architected lens turns sovereignty into five design questions, a useful framing for regulated European workloads.

item.title: Cloudflare Traces puts the whole request path in one trace
item.description: Tracing that starts at the edge and continues into your origin over W3C and OpenTelemetry standards closes a common blind spot.
